name: Eastern Ong-Be
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Chen, Yen-ling. 2018. Proto-Ong-Be. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xvii+195 pp. hdl:10125/62511 (ScholarSpace, open access). Supporting: Xin Shibiao 辛世彪. 2022. 1892年庄延龄记录的临高语海口石山话. 民族语文 2022(6): 26-41 (image PDF).
catalog_locator: Chen 2018 p. 22 (end of sec. 2.2); p. 65 (sec. 3.1); p. 66 (sec. 3.1); pp. 69-71 (Tables 35, 38, 41: tones of Longtang, Yongxing, Changliu); p. 156 (sec. 6.6, remark on stress in monosyllabic tonal languages; this entry's source list's 'p. 157' is off by one); p. 9 (intelligibility tests, Eastern vs. Western). Xin 2022 (p. 37) for the 轻声 remark.
catalog_quote: [p. 22] All modern Ong-Be varieties are monosyllabic and tonal. No consonant clusters are allowed in the onset or coda. No phonemic vowel length distinction has been attested. [p. 65] The syllable structure of modern Ong-Be varieties is canonically CV(C)T, a pattern which lacks the vowel length distinction. ... With respect to suprasegmental features, there are six basic tone categories in Ong-Be (A1, A2, BC1, BC2, D1, and D2), four of which are non-checked tones (A1, A2, BC1, BC2) and two are checked tones (D1 and D2, which only occur in syllables ending in a stop coda). [p. 66] ... the Ong-Be varieties spoken in Haikou City (including Qiongshan County) form three subdivisions, all of which belong to Eastern Ong-Be. Longqiao, Longquan, and Longtang form one group because they all show further tonal splits in tones A1, D1 and D2. Yongxing and Shishan form another group because tonal splits are only attested in tone D1. Changliu, by contrast, has no further tonal split at all. As for the Ong-Be varieties spoken in northeastern Chengmai County, I use Laocheng ... [p. 156, sec. 6.6] Stress and reduplication serve as key witnesses for this distinction in polysyllabic languages with a rich morphology such as Tibetan languages. However, in monosyllabic tonal languages where full reduplication is the norm, reduplication does not provide much information on the status of a vocalic element.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Eastern Ong-Be varieties (Longtang, Yongxing, Changliu, Shishan, Laocheng) are monosyllabic lexical-tone languages (6-9 tones per variety, every syllable CV(C)+Tone); the source gives full tone inventories but makes no statement about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Related prosodic facts from the opened sources: positional tone sandhi in non-final syllables of compounds (Xin 2022: 连读变调, blocked in predicate-complement and subject-predicate structures; Chen 2018:35 on Shishan Tone A2 sandhi form), and one weakened numeral-classifier form whose second syllable 'may also be neutral-tone (轻声)' (Xin 2022:37, Shishan).
new_statements.domain_note: Monosyllabic citation forms with lexical tone; no word- or phrase-level stress domain is discussed in any opened source.
new_statements.identity_note: qion1238 'Eastern Ong-Be' is a dialect-level node under Lingao/Ong-Be (ling1270; ISO onb). Chen 2018's first-hand data are from Longtang (Qiongshan District), Yongxing and Changliu (Xiuying District, Haikou) — all explicitly classed by her as Eastern Ong-Be (p. 66); Xin 2022 describes Shishan (Xiuying District), 'Eastern dialect group'. The sibling Western node is ling1262 (Lincheng/Xinying; Hashimoto 1980). Savina/Haudricourt 1965 'Bê' = Changliu, i.e. also Eastern Ong-Be.

tone_statements.citation: 王文敏 Wang Wenmin & 朱晓农 Zhu Xiaonong. 2022. 从声调类型看临高语短调的演化 [A study on the evolution of checked tones in the Lingao language: the tonotype perspective]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2022(1): 38-49.
tone_statements.quote: 本文用演化比较法对临高语51个点短调的地理分布、共时差异及其演化历程进行研究。根据短调的地理分布和共时差异，将临高语分为东、中、西3个方言区。中区为T7高T8低的2个短调，但T8的气声消失。东区为T7高T8低且T8保留气声，因声调分化和引进形成3-5类短调；短调分化的原因是增生借词调T9{55}导致T7降低及连串变化。西区为T7低T8高的2个短调，音高发生翻转，原因可能是由发声态变化引起的，即T8产生张声导致基频上升，使低音翻转为高音。
tone_statements.translation: Using the evolutionary-comparative method we study the geographic distribution, synchronic variation and evolution of the short (checked) tones at 51 Lingao points. By the short tones Lingao divides into eastern, central and western dialect areas. The central area has 2 short tones, T7 high and T8 low, but T8 has lost its breathy voice. The eastern area has T7 high, T8 low with T8 keeping breathy voice, and through tone splitting and borrowing has 3-5 short-tone categories; the split was caused by the new loan tone T9 {55} lowering T7 and a chain of changes. The western area has 2 short tones with T7 low and T8 high, a pitch flip-flop probably caused by a phonation change: tense voice on T8 raised F0.
tone_statements.locator: p. 38 (abstract, as printed on the journal landing page); sec. 四 '东区分化型：琼山的短调分化' pp. 44-46
tone_statements.summary: Eastern Ong-Be checked syllables carry 3-5 short tones (T7, T7', T8, (T8'), loan T9, plus checked-ized T2 at Shishan), T7 high / T8 low with breathy T8, within the 8-12-tone systems of work 1.

tone_statements.citation: 王文敏 Wang Wenmin & 朱晓农 Zhu Xiaonong. 2020. 演化观中的临高语声调类型 [Tonotypes of the Lingao language: an evolutionary perspective]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2020(1): 11-26.
tone_statements.quote: 本文以 29 点海南临高语土语声调的第一手录音材料，在音节音系学和通用调型库框架中，从演化学的视角建立临高语的声调类型系统。临高语方言分临桥和琼山两个大区，中间一个过渡性的长澄小区。西面的临桥区 6 个声调，中间的长澄区 7 个声调，东面的琼山区 8 到 12 个声调，主要是多少不等地多了三个撇调(T1'、T7'、T8')和三个借词调(T5、T6、T9)，T10 的调位身份存疑。 ... 3）琼山区：8 至 12 个调类，下分府石片和三龙片。府石片分布于琼山区府城镇，及秀英区永兴镇、石山镇等地；三龙片分布于琼山区龙塘镇、龙华区龙泉镇、龙桥镇等地。 ... 这些调系里有 4 个低调即 T1、4、7、8，程度不等地带有气声。
tone_statements.translation: Using first-hand recordings of the tones of 29 Lingao localities on Hainan ... we set up the tonal typology of Lingao from an evolutionary perspective. Lingao dialects fall into two large areas, Linqiao and Qiongshan, with a small transitional Changcheng area between. The western Linqiao area has 6 tones, the central Changcheng area 7, the eastern Qiongshan area 8 to 12, mainly through three extra split tones (T1', T7', T8') and three loan tones (T5, T6, T9); the phonemic status of T10 is doubtful. ... 3) Qiongshan area: 8 to 12 tone categories, subdivided into the Fu-Shi piece (Fucheng town, Yongxing, Shishan) and the San-Long piece (Longtang, Longquan, Longqiao). ... In these systems four low tones, T1, 4, 7, 8, carry breathy voice to varying degrees.
tone_statements.locator: p. 11 (提要/abstract); p. 11-12 sec. 一 (dialect division); p. 17 sec. 四 (琼山区), with Figs. 6-10 and appendix tone-value table pp. 24-26
tone_statements.summary: Syllable-tone language; Eastern (Qiongshan/Haikou) varieties have 8-12 lexical tones (7 long + up to 5 checked/short), incl. split tones T1', T7', T8', Hainan-Min loan tones T5, T6, T9 and a breathy low register on T1/T4/T7/T8; Changliu 7 tones.

First-hand fieldwork phonologies of the Eastern varieties Longtang, Yongxing and Changliu (sec. 3.2 Haikou City, pp. 67-71: consonants, vowels, tone tables: Longtang 9 tones, Yongxing 7, Changliu 6), Laocheng after Zhang et al. 1985, Shishan after Xin 2011. p. 22: 'All modern Ong-Be varieties are monosyllabic and tonal.' p. 65: syllable canonically CV(C)T, six basic tone categories A1 A2 BC1 BC2 D1 D2.
